rationale: This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "WorkingCapital ShortDebt Funding Pressure" signal (MUL→MIN, oancf/at→oancf/sale) with identical legs and mechanism, so it tests no new economic idea and merely re-shuffles an already-evaluated result.

Sign conventions and internal logic are coherent, but it is the archived "InventoryBuild CashMargin Erosion" signal with one extra short-debt-trend term bolted into a SUMRANK — an incremental splice of two prior legs rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the added term dilutes the leg that actually produced the -2.89 alpha.

The receivables-build leg is correctly signed and the conditioner (cash-conversion instability plus rising short-term debt reliance) is a genuinely different quality dimension from the previously tested sales-deceleration and revenue-vs-cash-trend versions, though the volatility leg partly recycles the known cash-flow-volatility anomaly.

Both legs are taken verbatim from archived signals (ABS(aoloch/at) and the VOL(oancf)−VOL(ni) smoothing gap), each of which already produced positive alphas directly opposite the hypothesized negative sign, so this recombination has a low prior and adds no new information.

The second leg (trend in ni/at minus trend in oancf/at) is a repackaging of the well-known accrual anomaly and is mechanically correlated with the tax-payable accrual leg, so the "interaction" largely double-counts one published effect rather than crossing distinct themes.

"Low working-capital accrual × durable cash margin" has now been tested three times in the archive (MA, TREND, and MIN-composite variants) and consistently delivered negative alphas against the positive expected sign; swapping MA for TS_MIN is a cosmetic variant that does not diagnose why the pattern keeps inverting.
